The bundled visual descriptor samples routine newly visible people/objects every four simulated seconds. That is at most about 67 ms at 1× and 8.3 ms at 8×. This is an authored attention-acquisition cadence, not a restriction on current vision, a renderer frame rate, or an acoustic timer. Brief visual-only appearances between samples can be missed; no already acquired evidence is removed. Current inspection, targeting and every committed event's audience use exact current geometry. Speech reception, intelligible fragments and source identity remain event-time decisions, never batched together or deferred to this sample.

Body contact keeps one-second native boundaries. A new command/restore root, changed sensor rules or membership, and perception restriction changes force fresh evaluation rather than reusing an old exposure proof. The generic vision descriptor's optional `acquisitionIntervalSeconds` accepts positive whole simulated seconds; omission retains one-second acquisition. The base world's four-second default is reversible tuning. See [native execution slices](../../performance.md#native-execution-slices) for snapshot batching; sampling does not increase a source's physical reach or confer unseen knowledge.

The base world uses bounded health, fullness and energy attributes, initial values and concern descriptions from `packages/domain/src/worlds/base/attributes.ts`. Sight in `senses.ts` defaults to 28 world units. Ordinary speech is clear to roughly 10 metres in the authored unobstructed reference conditions; [hearing](../../hearing-and-speech.md) applies continuous source levels, attenuation and receiver thresholds. Their detectors apply geometry and receiver scope; naming a sense never grants an actor all world knowledge.

The server may share one draft across up to four already-due one-second physical steps, only after an established immutable exposure boundary and no farther than the next authored visual-acquisition sample. It never waits for a fuller batch. Each substep keeps native actor order, RNG, needs, movement and status-rate integration; logical sequence, commitments and conversation continuity settle at the original one-second boundaries. Any allocated occurrence/transition or changed observer-perception restriction ends the slice early. Body-contact worlds, mutable inputs and new command/restore roots retain single-step boundaries.

Only redundant snapshot materialization is batched. Speech commands remain separate atomic utterances with event-time audiences and stored listener-specific evidence; receiver lists are never capped. Native participant candidates omit only provably absent work and refresh after a nested command; they do not suppress movement or sensing. The host accounts actual simulated seconds returned by a slice, retains the unprocessed debt, and releases mutation ownership after its existing soft work budget. `native.slice` measures a whole call, not an invented per-substep latency. A single slice can exceed the soft time budget; hardware and workload qualification remains required.

The accepted base-world acquisition compromise is owned by [routine visual discovery](worlds/base/survival.md#routine-visual-discovery). Other vision policies retain their chosen cadence. Publication and durability retain their existing host cadence and transaction owner; provider work is never moved into the native lane.

**Current policy:** [Routine visual discovery](../worlds/base/survival.md#routine-visual-discovery). Native batching is governed separately by [execution slices](../performance.md#native-execution-slices); neither policy relaxes speech, interaction authorization or privacy.
**Why revisit:** Four simulated seconds trades potentially missed brief visual-only exposure for responsive accelerated play. It is a world-policy tuning choice, not a universal sensory law.

**Review trigger:** Fast stealth/combat, materially faster movement, timed hiding, different clock ratios or playtesting demonstrates missed meaningful sightings. Reevaluate the cadence or add event-driven acquisition under EPR rather than enlarging hearing reach or dropping listeners. Other worlds can already choose their own descriptor interval.
**Decision authority:** The game/design owner, with EPR/SW and performance owners; Mike authorized this task's reasonable performance tradeoffs.

## September 25 — Hearing integration and native execution slices

The hearing branch integrates the new implementation/documentation rules and current main's physical-contact and nonblocking-memory behavior. D63 retains speech re-authoring while upstream D61/D62 retain scale/recall ownership. Native execution may share snapshots across bounded physical substeps; it does not batch utterances or cap recipients. The base world adopts a four-simulated-second routine visual-acquisition cadence to reduce accelerated-play overhead; current geometric queries and acoustic evidence remain exact. Brief visual-only appearances between samples can be missed. The accepted compromise is tracked under [RP03](maintainers/revisitable-policies.md#rp03--base-world-visual-discovery-cadence); [performance](performance.md#native-execution-slices) and [HE05](maintainers/hearing-and-speech.md#he05--runtime-and-performance-qualification) own mechanism and qualification. This entry is not an end-to-end 8× capacity claim.
